text_blocks.snippet: A tourist visa (B-1/B-2) allows for a maximum stay of 6 months (180 days) per visit, regardless of the visa's validity period. While the visa itself may be valid for up to 10 years, the authorized stay in the U.S. is determined by the Customs and Border Protection (CBP) officer upon entry and is noted on your I-94 form.

list.title: Visa Validity:
list.snippet: A B-1/B-2 visa is typically valid for 10 years, allowing you to travel to the U.S. multiple times within that period.

list.title: Authorized Stay:
list.snippet: However, each time you enter the U.S., the CBP officer determines how long you can stay, usually up to 6 months (180 days).

list.title: I-94 Form:
list.snippet: The specific length of your authorized stay is recorded on your I-94 form, either as a date or "D/S" (duration of status).

list.title: Overstaying:
list.snippet: It is crucial to leave the U.S. before the end date on your I-94, even if your visa is still valid, as overstaying can negatively impact future travel plans and visa renewals.

text_blocks.snippet: To obtain a U.S. tourist visa, also known as a visitor visa (B-2 or combined B1/B2), you'll need to apply online through the U.S. Department of State (.gov). The first step is completing the online nonimmigrant visa application (Form DS-160). After submitting the application, you'll need to pay the fee and schedule an interview at the nearest U.S. embassy or consulate.

list.title: 1. Determine if you need a visa:
list.snippet: Check if your country participates in the Visa Waiver Program (VWP). If it does, you may be eligible for an Electronic System for Travel Authorization (ESTA) instead of a visa.

list.title: 2. Complete the DS-160 form:
list.snippet: This is the online application form for nonimmigrant visas. You'll need to provide information about yourself, your travel plans, and your background.

list.title: 3. Pay the visa application fee:
list.snippet: The fee varies depending on the type of visa.

list.title: 4. Schedule an interview:
list.snippet: Once you've completed the DS-160 and paid the fee, you can schedule an interview at the nearest U.S. embassy or consulate.

list.title: 5. Attend the interview:
list.snippet: You'll need to bring your passport, the DS-160 confirmation page, and any supporting documents requested by the consular officer.

list.title: 6. Await the decision:
list.snippet: After the interview, the consular officer will make a decision on your visa application.

text_blocks.snippet: Important things to keep in mind:

list.title: Passport validity:
list.snippet: Your passport must be valid for at least six months beyond your intended stay in the U.S.

list.title: Supporting documents:
list.snippet: You may need to provide proof of funds, a travel itinerary, and evidence of ties to your home country.

list.title: Interview preparation:
list.snippet: Be prepared to answer questions about your travel plans, your reasons for visiting the U.S., and your ties to your home country.

text_blocks.snippet: Applying for a visa is an important process and it's crucial to follow all instructions carefully. If you have any questions, you can find more information on the U.S. Department of State (.gov) website.
